needs_human.note: The section-level blur handler clears the browse point for every pointer type. I3 says a touch or pen browse point stays until a tile or card is tapped, the playback jumps, the section collapses or the file changes. The spec lists "focus leaves the section" only under Keyboard (§1 step 9).

A mouse browse point is not cleared when the pointer leaves the browser window directly from a child of the section. onPointerOut needs a non-null relatedTarget, and onPointerLeave needs target === currentTarget (Presenter.tsx:164-174). This matters only when the section touches the window edge.; The WS effect does not check policy.enabled. A visual_video event for the current file, while expanded with the policy off or still loading, would fetch visual-index and draw Visual Index parts, against I9's policy-off clause. Unlikely in normal use, because a policy-off drive should emit no such events.; After re-expanding, a stale global lastEvent for the same file triggers a second visual-index request, which supersedes the initial one. The visible result is the same.
